why: Shared initial preference should close early without repetitive filler.
Independent preferences should narrow without controller-authored concessions.
Low-stubbornness participants can visibly accept or switch.
A valid majority must close without unanimity repair.
The sole blocker never switches or votes away from its option.
A direct question must be answered and receive a real issue outcome.
A concern owner may explicitly maintain an objection.
A low-stubbornness concern owner can evaluate a mitigation, resolve the issue, and accept the option.
Protocol must run with no visible moderator turns.
Prepared flight facts and comparisons must remain grounded.
Unequal engagement should yield unequal voluntary participation.
Comparable voluntary contributions should reflect word-budget differences.
A committed preference switch must be visible in the transcript.
Different personal priorities should produce different structured reasons and occasional relevant personal context.
A split may use one complete re-vote and then close unresolved.
